name: Leg Press
summary: A machine press that loads the quads and glutes with the back supported, so you can train the legs hard with little demand on balance or the trunk.
setup: Adjust the seat so your knees are bent at about 90 degrees or a little more when the sled is at the bottom.
Sit with your back and hips flat against the pad and place your feet about shoulder width on the platform, mid-height.
Grip the handles and unlock the safety handles or stops as shown on your machine.
Press the sled up to a near-straight leg position to start, without locking out.
execution: Take a breath and lower the sled slowly by bending your knees and hips.
Stop when your knees are at about 90 degrees or when your hips are about to lift off the pad.
Keep your whole foot on the platform and your knees tracking in line with your toes.
Press the platform away, exhaling, until your legs are almost straight.
Re-lock the safety stops before getting out of the machine.
cues: Hips and back stay on the pad
mistakes: Lowering too deep so the hips curl off the pad and the lower back rounds: limit the range to where the pelvis stays flat.
Locking the knees hard at the top: stop just short of full lockout and keep tension on the muscles.
Knees caving in: push the knees out toward the little toes and lighten the weight.
Bouncing out of the bottom with a heavy load: slow down and use a weight you can control.
